title: Small-scale protocol for magnetic coagulation testing
author: Kristianto, Saputera, et al.

steps.title: Prepare Congo red synthetic wastewater
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g Congo red powder (Sigma‑Aldrich), dissolve in distilled water to make a 1 g L⁻¹ stock solution; pipette 20 mL of this stock into distilled water and dilute to 1 L to obtain a 50 mg L⁻¹ working solution, then adjust the pH to the desired value with 0.1 N HCl or 0.1 N NaOH.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1 g Congo red powder.
Dissolve in distilled water to prepare a 1 g L⁻¹ stock.
Pipette 20 mL of stock and dilute to 1 L for 50 mg L⁻¹ working solution.
Adjust pH with 0.1 N HCl or 0.1 N NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare Moringa oleifera crude extract
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 g dried Moringa oleifera seed kernel powder, add to 100 mL of 1 M NaCl solution, stir at 100 rpm for 30 min, centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 10 min, filter the supernatant, and use the filtrate immediately as fresh coagulant.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 5 g dried Moringa seed kernel powder.
Add powder to 100 mL 1 M NaCl solution.
Stir with magnetic stirrer at 100 rpm for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 10 min.
Filter the supernatant to remove particulates.
Use the resulting extract directly; prepare fresh before each experiment.

steps.title: Prepare magnetic coagulant suspension
steps.instruction: Measure 20 mL of the Moringa extract, add 60 mg Fe₃O₄ nanopowder (Aldrich) to achieve 3 mg mL⁻¹, sonicate in an Elmasonic S300H ultrasonic bath for 5 min, and keep the suspension for use as magnetic coagulant.

substeps.instruction: Measure 20 mL of Moringa seed extract.
Add 60 mg Fe₃O₄ nanopowder (target 3 mg mL⁻¹).
Sonicate in Elmasonic S300H bath for 5 min.
Use the resulting suspension in subsequent coagulation experiments.

steps.title: Conduct conventional jar test coagulation
steps.instruction: In a 1 L beaker place 500 mL of the 50 mg L⁻¹ Congo red solution, adjust pH to 3 with 0.1 M HCl or 0.1 M NaOH, add magnetic coagulant at 20 mL L⁻¹ (10 mL for 500 mL), mix rapidly at 200 rpm for 3 min then slowly at 60 rpm for 30 min, let settle for 1 h with neodymium magnets beneath the beaker, and collect supernatant from 2–3 cm below the surface.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL of 50 mg L⁻¹ Congo red solution in a 1 L beaker.
Adjust solution pH to 3 using 0.1 M HCl or 0.1 M NaOH.
Add magnetic coagulant at 20 mL L⁻¹ (10 mL for this volume).
Rapid mixing at 200 rpm for 3 min.
Slow mixing at 60 rpm for 30 min.
Allow mixture to settle for 1 h with external neodymium magnets beneath the beaker.
Collect supernatant from 2–3 cm below the surface for analysis.

steps.title: Perform miniaturized coagulation assay
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of pH‑3 Congo red wastewater to a test tube, pipette 100 µL magnetic coagulant, vortex with a Thermolyne type 37,600 mixer for 10 s, settle 10 min with a 40 mm × 3 mm neodymium magnet (65 mT) placed beside the tube, then withdraw 3 mL supernatant for analytical measurement.

substeps.instruction: Pour 5 mL of Congo red wastewater (pH 3) into a test tube.
Pipette 100 µL magnetic coagulant.
Mix using a Thermolyne type 37,600 vortex mixer for 10 s.
Allow the mixture to settle for 10 min with a neodymium magnet (diameter 40 mm, height 3 mm, flux density 65 mT) placed beside the tube.
Carefully withdraw 3 mL of supernatant for analysis.

steps.title: Measure dye concentration and calculate removal
steps.instruction: Measure the initial concentration (Ci) with a Thermo Scientific Genesys 150 spectrophotometer at 575 nm using distilled water as blank, repeat after coagulation to obtain final concentration (Cf), and compute % removal = (Ci‑Cf)/Ci × 100.

substeps.instruction: Set spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific Genesys 150) wavelength to 575 nm.
Measure initial Congo red concentration (Ci) using distilled water as blank.
After coagulation, measure final concentration (Cf) under the same conditions.
Calculate percentage removal: % removal = (Ci − Cf)/Ci × 100.

steps.title: Observe flocs by optical microscopy
steps.instruction: Immediately after settling, collect a drop of sample with a micropipette, place on a clean glass slide, cover with a coverslip without bubbles, observe under a Rehaze Microscope Binocular XSZ‑107BN at 400×, adjust focus and illumination, capture images, and analyse floc fractal dimension using ImageJ 1.54g with FracLac 2.5 (box‑counting method).

substeps.instruction: Collect a drop of the settled sample with a micropipette.
Place the drop on a clean glass microscope slide.
Gently cover with a coverslip, avoiding air bubbles and excessive pressure.
Observe under Rehaze Microscope Binocular XSZ‑107BN at 400× magnification.
Adjust focus and illumination for clear visualization.
Capture images with the camera‑mounted microscope.
Analyze 2‑D fractal dimension of flocs using ImageJ 1.54g with FracLac 2.5 (box‑counting method).
